identity.kind: used car engine with attached transmission/transaxle assembly (seller claims Lexus IS250)

claims.evidence: No badge, engine code plate, or VIN sticker is legible in photo 0 to confirm this is a Lexus IS250 engine specifically; the assembly could be any similar V6/transaxle unit.

risks.risk: Engine model/displacement cannot be confirmed, which drives most of the value difference (e.g., 2GR-FE vs 4GR-FE vs a different make entirely).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code plate/stamp on the block, or a VIN plate/sticker if still attached to a cut section.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unidentified generic used engine assembly, not confirmed as Lexus IS250

risks.risk: Whether the engine runs or has good compression is unknown; a pulled yard engine photo alone shows nothing about function.
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine being started and idling, or a compression test reading on camera.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for-parts condition

risks.risk: Mileage and prior accident/flood history are unverifiable from a static photo.
risks.proof: Photo of the donor vehicle's odometer or a history/import document matching the engine tag.

risks.risk: Completeness of the assembly (sensors, wiring harness, turbo/accessories if any) cannot be confirmed from one angle.
risks.proof: Additional photos from front, rear, and both sides showing all harness connectors and accessory brackets intact.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete, missing ancillary parts

risks.risk: Internal wear (bearings, timing components) is invisible from an external shot.
risks.proof: Borescope photo/video of cylinder bores or a teardown photo.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine code stamp/plate or VIN tag confirming make and model.
Video of the engine running/idling with sound.
Photos from additional angles (front, rear, both sides) showing full wiring harness and accessories.
Any paperwork (import permit, donor vehicle registration) linking this engine to a Lexus IS250.
response.reason: The photo shows a generic used engine/transmission assembly with no legible brand or model marking, so the Lexus IS250 claim is unverified and the specific model that would set the price cannot be confirmed from what's shown.
